nodes.title: Measured on 437 promoted patches: 1.6% touch tests, 1.6% touch the gate or verifier, 2.1% touch the runner scripts
nodes.body:
The w3-falsify-verifier-decay node says the empirical question that decides whether Goodhart applies to us is answerable: count how often an accepted edit changes the verifier or the tests. Counted it. Across 437 stored patch artifacts, 7 patches (1.6%) touch a tests/ path, 7 (1.6%) touch src/exec/verifier.js or src/gate/, and 9 (2.1%) touch scripts/test-all.mjs, scripts/verify.mjs or scripts/e2e.mjs. The offenders are concentrated: loom-chaos (4 patches) and loom-self4 (2) account for six of the seven test touches, and those campaigns had no no-test-edit check.

Interpretation, and its limit: at this rate there is no optimisation pressure toward verifier hacking in our loop, which is the opposite of the SWE-Bench finding (28.57% hacked before a judge was added). The reason is structural rather than virtuous -- the loop is 62 short campaigns each optimising against a frozen command, and a campaign that edits its own verifier would have to be working on a task whose brief asks for that (two of ours literally did: the self-test authoring campaigns). So the honest statement is that our task framing keeps the Goodhart surface out of reach, not that our gate resists it. The moment a campaign objective becomes 'make the suite green' rather than 'make this specific behaviour correct', the 1.6% becomes the thing to watch, and the existing no-test-edit check is the only guard.

Actionable asymmetry: verification hardening (mutation auditing, exp-mut-001) is cheap and unmeasured, while the hacking it protects against is currently absent. So mutation auditing should be run as a diagnostic on the verifier we ship, not as a per-round guard.

edges.note: Answers the empirical question that node poses: our accepted-edit hacking rate is 1.6%, not 28.6%.
Mutation auditing is worth running once on the shipped verifier rather than as a per-round guard.
Narrows verifier measurement to a one-time diagnostic plus a standing no-test-edit check.
